candidates.exact_span: It is proposed that the permit be reissued for a 5-year term following regulations promulgated at 40 CFR §122.46(a).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether and when the reissued permit takes effect determines which permit term, effective dates, and condition set govern limit and monitoring applicability across Federal FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: The previous permit will be expired on October 31, 2021.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The stated expiration date of the prior permit affects which permit framework is in force during FY2025 when read together with administrative continuation, changing which limits, monitoring requirements, and missing-evidence rules apply.

candidates.exact_span: The existing permit is administratively continued until this permit is issued.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Administrative continuation means FY2025 may be evaluated under the prior permit rather than the reissued permit until issuance, changing applicable numeric limits, monitoring obligations, and how absent results are interpreted.

candidates.exact_span: NPDES permit limits are developed that meet the more stringent of either technology-based effluent limitation guidelines, numerical and/or narrative water quality standard-based effluent limits, or the previous permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The more-stringent-of selection rule determines which limit source controls each parameter; different readings of TBEL, WQBEL, prior-permit, or narrative versus numerical limits change the enforceable limit used for measurement comparison.

candidates.exact_span: Technology-based effluent limitations are established in the proposed draft permit for TSS and BOD.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Assigns TSS and BOD to technology-based effluent limitations, affecting which numeric limits apply to reported measurements and which parameter-specific monitoring obligations are tied to those limits.

candidates.exact_span: Water quality-based effluent limitations are established in the proposed draft permit for E. coli bacteria, pH and TRC.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Assigns E. coli, pH, and TRC to water-quality-based effluent limitations, affecting applicable limit values for compliance comparison and the monitoring requirements associated with those parameters.

candidates.exact_span: Regulations promulgated at 40 CFR §122.44 (a) require TBELs to be placed in NPDES permits based on ELGs where applicable, on BPJ in the absence of guidelines, or on a combination of the two.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether limits derive from ELGs, BPJ, or a combination changes the technology-based numeric limits selected for comparison against reported measurements.

candidates.exact_span: In the absence of promulgated guidelines for the discharge, permit conditions may be established using BPJ procedures.
candidates.computation_change_reason: If no promulgated ELGs apply to this discharge, BPJ-derived limits rather than guideline limits govern, changing the applicable numeric discharge limits.

candidates.exact_span: EPA establishes limitations based on the following technology-based controls: BPT, BCT, and BAT.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The applicable technology level among BPT, BCT, and BAT determines which treatment-based numeric limits are imposed and therefore which limits are used in compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: BPT - The first level of technology-based standards generally based on the average of the best existing performance facilities within an industrial category or subcategory.
candidates.computation_change_reason: If BPT is the governing technology level, interpretation of this standard and its category basis affects the derived numeric TBEL values used to evaluate reported measurements.
